questions.question: Which substitution strategy produced the paper's strongest α-glucosidase inhibitors among the fused pyrimidine derivatives?

options.A: Replacing the position-4 carbonyl with amino-bridged substituents
options.B: N-alkylation at position 4 with simple ethyl groups only
options.C: Replacing the phenoxy ring with a saturated sugar mimic
options.D: Thionation of the pyrimidine carbonyl in every derivative

questions.rationale: The authors associate strong inhibition in 6a–6i with amino-bridge substitution at position 4, whereas most N-alkylated products were weak.
questions.evidence_quote: the aminobridge substitution of the pyrimidine ring at position 4 is responsible for the strong inhibitory activity.

questions.question: What did screening at a fixed 100 µg/mL show about the distribution of activities across the 25 compounds?

options.A: Eight compounds exceeded 50% average inhibition and were advanced to IC50 determination
options.B: All 25 compounds exceeded 60% and were advanced to docking
options.C: Only two compounds exceeded 50%, and the remaining compounds were inactive
options.D: Six compounds exceeded 50%, but no IC50 values were calculated

questions.rationale: The initial assay was triplicated at equal concentration; eight compounds crossed 50% average inhibition and were assessed further.
questions.evidence_quote: The eight compounds (out of the 25 tested) that exhibited more than 50% of the average percent inhibition were further evaluated and their IC 50 values compared to that of acarbose.

questions.question: How did compounds 2a and 2d compare with compound 3 in IC50, and what were their substituent identities?
questions.rationale: The text gives the IC50 values for compound 3 and the ethyl and 2-methylbenzyl N-alkylated compounds in that order.
questions.evidence_quote: the IC 50 of compound 3 was 167.82 µM and those of compound 2a and 2d were 304.13 µM and 173.83 µM, respectively

questions.question: Which docking result most strongly distinguished compound 6h from the other synthesized derivatives?

options.A: It had the lowest reported docking binding energy, approximately −10.56 kcal/mol
options.B: It had the highest binding energy, approximately −8.12 kcal/mol
options.C: It formed no hydrogen bonds but contacted ten active-site residues
options.D: Its binding energy was −9.17 kcal/mol, weaker than 6b

questions.rationale: The authors report −10.56 kcal/mol as the lowest energy among docked derivatives, consistent with a stable complex.
questions.evidence_quote: the binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol) among the energies of the docked derivatives

questions.question: Which three α-glucosidase residues were reported to hydrogen-bond with compound 6h?
questions.rationale: The docking analysis identifies three residues interacting with 6h through hydrogen bonds, stabilizing its complex.
questions.evidence_quote: three residues appear to interact with compound 6h, Ala234, Arg552 and Asp469, to which 6h can establish hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: What role did Trp329 play in the docking interpretation?

options.A: It formed a hydrophobic interaction that helped direct the ligand's binding conformation
options.B: It formed one of the three hydrogen bonds that reduced 6h binding energy
options.C: It prevented acarbose from binding by occupying the catalytic site
options.D: It formed a covalent bond with the pyrimidine nitrogen

questions.rationale: Trp329 is described as making hydrophobic contact with 2a and 6h and directing their binding conformation.
questions.evidence_quote: Trp329 can also form hydrophobic bonds with compounds 2a and 6h as in the case of acarbose, which is responsible for the binding conformation of the compounds in the active site.

questions.question: How was α-glucosidase activity measured in the microplate assay?

options.A: p-NPG hydrolysis was followed by absorbance at 405 nm before and after 30 min at 37°C
options.B: Glucose release was measured at 590 nm after 10 min at room temperature
options.C: Acarbose displacement was measured by fluorescence after 45 min at 4°C
options.D: The enzyme's NADH consumption was measured at 340 nm for 30–45 min

questions.rationale: The assay added p-NPG substrate, recorded initial absorbance at 405 nm, incubated for 30 minutes at 37°C and measured again.
questions.evidence_quote: The reaction was incubated for 30 min. at 37 °C and the absorbance was then measured.

questions.question: Which synthetic transformation converted compound 5 into hydrazone derivatives 6g and 6h?

options.A: Hydrazinolysis to 6f followed by condensation with aldehydes in ethanol
options.B: N-alkylation with alkyl halides in DMF and potassium carbonate
options.C: Thionation with P2S5 in pyridine followed by benzylation
options.D: Reaction with hydroxylamine hydrochloride in boiling pyridine

questions.rationale: Compound 5 was first converted to hydrazine 6f, then reacted with aldehydes to form hydrazones 6g and 6h.
questions.evidence_quote: Hydrazinolysis of 5 in boiling ethanol produced the corresponding compound 6f, which upon treatment with equimolar amounts of aldehydes resulted in the formation of hydrazone derivatives 6g and 6h

questions.question: What was the main limitation of the N-alkylated position-4 derivatives compared with the amino-bridged series?

options.A: Most showed weak inhibition; only 2a and 2d exceeded 50% average inhibition
options.B: They all inhibited more strongly than acarbose but could not be docked
options.C: They were not soluble in assay buffer and no inhibition data were obtained
options.D: Only 2a was active, while 2d had no measurable activity

questions.rationale: The N-alkylated derivatives generally showed weak activity, with ethyl 2a and 2-methylbenzyl 2d as the two exceptions over 50%.
questions.evidence_quote: Only two N-alkylated derivatives (ethyl and 2-methylbenzyl) showed more than 50% average percent inhibition (50.36% and 57.48%, respectively).

questions.question: What comparison with acarbose did the authors report for compounds 6d and 6h?

options.A: Both had lower IC50 values and stronger inhibitory activity than acarbose
options.B: Both had higher IC50 values and weaker activity than acarbose
options.C: Only 6h had a lower IC50; 6d was inactive
options.D: They matched acarbose in IC50 but differed only in docking energy

questions.rationale: The conclusion explicitly states that 6d and 6h showed significant inhibition with lower IC50 values than the reference drug.
questions.evidence_quote: Compounds 6d and 6h showed a significant inhibitory activity against α-glycosidase with lower IC 50 values than that of acarbose.
